text:
ajay: ran a full night of microbenchmarks for the hybrid fused-paged kernel + banked KV layout, and the numbers are... weird. lower memory but worse p99 for some seq lengths. posting raw results and a short repro

ajay: benchmark snippet:
```
model: mix-7b
kernels: fused-paged-v1, flash3-optim
layouts: banked-kv, split-kv
batch: 8
seq: [512,1024,1536]
results (tokens/s, p99 ms, gpu mem peak):
  seq=512  fused-paged: 320k, 22ms, 8.6G  | flash3: 340k, 21ms, 9.3G
  seq=1024 fused-paged: 210k, 38ms, 9.8G  | flash3: 230k, 34ms, 11.2G
  seq=1536 fused-paged: 155k, 62ms, 12.0G  | flash3: 162k, 58ms, 13.1G
notes: banked-kv reduced mem but p99 regressed at mid seq lengths. float16 dtype used for all runs.
```

ajay: repro command: `python perf/run_kv_bench.py --model mix-7b --kernel fused-paged-v1 --layout banked --pad 64 --dtype float16 --batch 8 --seq 1024`

maria: can you paste the nvprof/NVTX ranges? also which cuda/cudnn/driver? might be a bank conflict or extra memcpy at page boundary. :thinking_face:

ajay: driver 535.54, cuda 12.2. nvtx shows an extra memcpy around KV page rollover for banked layout. small snippet:
```
NVTX: [KV_PAGE_FILL] 120ms -> [GPU_MEMCPY] 127ms -> [ATTN_KERNEL:fused-paged] 132ms
vs flash3: [KV_PAGE_FILL] 118ms -> [ATTN_KERNEL:flash3] 120ms
```

ajay: seems fused-paged triggers a fallback copy when a KV chunk crosses the bank boundary, which costs ~6-8ms in our test.

maria: interesting. iirc banked layout uses 256B stride per bank, but our allocator sometimes gives 128B start offsets for small allocations which causes the crossing. can you try padding to 256B and re-run?

ajay: tried pad=256, p99 for seq=1024 improved from 38ms -> 30ms, throughput +9%. memory went up ~200MB. so padding helps but eats some mem.

lina: is this specific to float16? what about bfloat16 path?

taylor: ran quick loop this morning: bfloat16 path avoids the memcpy/fallback in fused-paged, p99 matches flash3, but overall token throughput is 3-4% lower on large seq because of extra compute in the bfloat path. numbers: seq=1024 fused-paged-bf16 225k tok/s, p99 35ms.

sam: we should probably update kernel selection heuristics: if layout==banked and start_offset % 256 != 0 -> prefer flash3 or force pad. Also: heuristic based on seq length and batch to choose fused-paged vs flash3. low-seq fused-paged wins, mid-seq tie, high-seq flash3 slightly better.

maria: agree. also add a quick runtime check in the allocator to align KV rows to 256 if fused-paged is chosen. cheap and effective. can we gate this behind a rollout flag for Dedicated?

ajay: i can prot a small patch: allocator ensures `base_addr % 256 == 0` when kernel==fused-paged, else leave as-is. will create a canary in staging.

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: canary/staging -> eng-runtime-fused-paged-align  at 2026-03-11T09:30Z by ajay :rocket:

sam: also let's add a microbenchmark to CI that flips start offsets randomly to catch regressions. flag: `--random-offsets` in run_kv_bench.

maria: good. quick follow ups: 1) add NVTX ranges to logs for every KV page fill 2) record pad vs mem tradeoffs in perf dashboard 3) try smaller pad like 128 -> sometimes enough but not guaranteed.

ajay: will open PR with the allocator change + test harness. tagging taylor for perf regression check and sam for rollout plan.

taylor: i'll run a wider sweep across batches [1,2,4,8,16] and seqs [256..2048], check both float16 and bf16. will post a heatmap tomorrow.

maria: thanks all. this feels like a nice low-risk fix -> optimizer + allocator + heuristic. wins for mid-seq latency without huge mem cost. :thumbsup:

ajay: PR: https://git.redwood.internal/ri/runtime/pulls/4123 (draft) — includes pad heuristic, NVTX markers, and bench update. please review.

sam: noted. i'll add the CI microbench and a canary schedule for Dedicated clusters.

lina: FYI: sales asked about memory footprint delta for Dedicated customers. ajay pls include a short blurb in PR about worst-case mem + expected improvement ranges.

ajay: will do. thanks everyone.
